title: Choose the portfolio's visual world
question: The roll assigned Safelight Contact Sheet. Choose it, an alternate, the familiar category standard, or re-roll.

options.label: Safelight Contact Sheet
options.lineage: Black-and-white photographic contact sheets and the amber-lit printing darkroom
options.thesis: Let each project emerge from a deliberate, readable working sheet.
options.viewport: An amber field sheet opens on SmartAgri as one developed project record, with the next work visible below.
options.case: Path: scan the project sheet, open a project record, then move through experience, study, and contact. Signature: a reversible, keyboard-accessible exposure strip selects a project without concealing its title or details. Reach: the same numbered record grammar carries across projects, work history, and mobile layouts.
options.risk: The darkroom metaphor can obscure the work; keep project names, roles, and descriptions at full contrast and make every interaction reversible.

raised.raise: Project records visibly connect the stated problem, approach, and listed technologies without animating or rewriting their factual content.
Give each project one focused editorial field instead of flattening the work into a grid of interchangeable cards.

options.label: Field Journal
options.lineage: Field notebooks and West African science-reporting broadsheets
options.thesis: Read the work as a sequence of grounded engineering field notes.
options.viewport: A dated field-note masthead introduces the SmartAgri entry, its role, technologies, and the next project in sequence.
options.case: Path: browse the field index, read a project note, then continue to experience and contact. Signature: a pinned index number tracks the selected note and remains available on narrow screens. Reach: projects, experience, and study share one editorial record system.
options.risk: Field-report styling is familiar editorial territory; the work must lead rather than letting the notebook props take over.

options.label: Hand-Bent Neon Circuit
options.lineage: Hand-bent gas-discharge signage and continuous glass-tube circuits
options.thesis: Trace the projects as connected engineering decisions, not a bag of technologies.
options.viewport: A connected project path leads into SmartAgri's real description, team role, and technologies.
options.case: The circuit makes engineering and IoT immediately legible, but the neon-sign metaphor is less specific to this portfolio than the selected darkroom's deliberate project sequence.
options.risk: A familiar tech-circuit motif could overpower the actual project evidence.

options.label: Teletext Service
options.lineage: Broadcast teletext indexes and fixed character-cell grids
options.thesis: Navigate the portfolio as a numbered, always-legible index of work.
options.viewport: A broadcast-style project index gives SmartAgri a numbered entry and opens its full description in a stable reading area.
options.case: The page-number grammar makes navigation and project order unusually clear, while the broadcast idiom is less personally grounded than the assigned direction.
options.risk: A rigid grid and nostalgia can make long project descriptions cramped or inaccessible.

options.label: Variable Type Specimen
options.lineage: Printed type-foundry specimens and variable-font proof sheets
options.thesis: Make engineering identity visible through a precise, changing typographic specimen.
options.viewport: An oversized typographic name shares the opening with a clear project index and the SmartAgri record.
options.case: The specimen celebrates typographic craft and gives the developer a memorable signature, but it places type ahead of the work visitors came to explore.
options.risk: A variable-font control has no portfolio value unless it remains subtle and accessible.

options.label: Alphabet Storm
options.thesis: Let project language transform into a navigable field of ideas.
options.case: Kept: make a project's problem and approach read as a connected sequence; reject animated text that could compromise factual clarity.
options.kept: Semantic connections between a project's problem, approach, and named technologies.
options.risk: Transformed words can be difficult to scan and can change the meaning of factual copy.

options.label: Dungeon Tape J-card
options.lineage: Hand-drawn cassette inserts and photocopied tracklists
options.thesis: Give every project the intimacy of one carefully made, fold-out record.
options.case: Kept: each project deserves its own focused reading field, not a row of interchangeable cards.
options.kept: A project-first focus with a clear, persistent index.
options.risk: A cassette sleeve is an unfamiliar personal artifact for the portfolio's professional audience.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished, familiar developer portfolio with conventional page structure.
canonCard.viewport: A clear name, concise introduction, featured projects, and expected portfolio navigation.
canonCard.risk: Familiar by design; it does not distinguish the work through a durable visual system.
